recall_prompt: Say how you would do this one — say what you differentiate with respect to, and which single term needs the product rule.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Differentiate every term with respect to x
steps.margin_note: First mark. Six terms, so work along the equation left to right and differentiate each one before simplifying. Only 3xy needs the product rule; the constant 8 differentiates to 0.
steps.memory_tip: Every y you differentiate leaves a dy/dx attached to it. Here that happens three times: in y², in 2y, and inside the product 3xy.
lines: y is not given in terms of x on its own, so differentiate implicitly, term by term, with respect to x.
The term 3xy is a product of x and y, so it needs the product rule.

recall.must_convey: That every term is differentiated with respect to x, with the product rule on 3xy and a dy/dx from y² and from 2y.
accept: differentiate each term with respect to x treating y as a function of x
only the three x y term needs the product rule
y squared gives two y d y by d x
prati term ni x tho differentiate cheyyali, three x y ki product rule
the constant eight differentiates to zero
heard_as: two y d y by d x

steps.why: This is a conic, and solving it for y would bring in a square root that then has to be differentiated. Implicit differentiation avoids that and takes three lines.
common_mistakes: Writing d/dx(3xy) as 3y, which drops the 3x · dy/dx half of the product rule.
Differentiating 2y as 2 and losing the dy/dx factor.

steps.label: Collect the dy/dx terms and solve
steps.margin_note: Second mark. Three terms carry dy/dx: −3x, +2y and +2. Take them together, move the rest across, then divide.
steps.memory_tip: The bracket that multiplies dy/dx is 2y − 3x + 2, and what is left over is 3y − 4x − 1. Group first, divide last.
lines: Collect the dy/dx terms on one side:

recall.must_convey: That the three dy/dx terms are collected, giving dy/dx = (3y − 4x − 1)/(2y − 3x + 2).

steps.why: Three separate terms carry dy/dx, so the mark is for gathering all three and none of the others. Missing the lone +2(dy/dx) is the usual way this answer comes out wrong.
common_mistakes: Leaving the +2(dy/dx) term on the other side, giving 2y − 3x as the denominator.
Sign slips when the terms 4x, −3y and +1 are moved across.
